analysis: The change touches CI only: provider-tests.yml, the docs and changelog files. It does not touch provider runtime, the coordinator WebSocket contract, attestation or the prefix-cache code. Unit 2ec3deede6392fe0:8 (lines 1052-1460) contains the new "Choose this job's Actions cache" gating and the "Discard a damaged or unsafe cached .git" step. The gating sets CI_ACTIONS_CACHE=off on darkbloom-* runners without DARKBLOOM_CACHE_URL. Every cache restore and save step visible in this unit checks that flag, which reduces exposure of CI artifacts to GitHub's shared Actions cache. This is an improvement. The .git sanitizer blocks symlinks, hooks, fsmonitor, hooksPath and includes before any git command reads the cache. It is a denylist, so other code-executing config keys remain (one low finding). Cache writes are limited to master and dev pushes (SAVE_CACHES), so the practical exposure is small. The lane and routing changes move build and GPU jobs to the Darkbloom plane with a Blacksmith fallback. The security-relevant questions are runner trust and the plane's cache isolation, which are platform-owned and not visible here. The docs and changelog files are descriptive. No threat IDs map directly, because the change is outside the provider and coordinator threat boundaries. Only one hunk of the workflow was supplied in full, so the other changed ranges (route inputs, other job steps, provider-plan.yml, scripts/test-provider-ci-workflow.py, the BoundedBufferCache test helper) were not reviewed. I could not verify that every cache step in the other files is gated.

findings.detail: The new step discards a cached .git only if it has a symlink, a non-sample hook, or a config setting core.fsmonitor, core.hooksPath, include.* or includeIf.*. It says the restored .git "runs nothing", but the check is incomplete. Config keys such as filter.<name>.smudge/clean/process (paired with a .git/info/attributes file, which is not inspected), core.sshCommand, core.pager, core.askpass, credential.helper, diff.external, gpg.program, alias.* and uploadpack.packObjectsHook can still run commands or redirect git. The following actions/checkout and git operations read that config. A poisoned cache entry, for example one from a compromised push to master or dev, which are the only refs that save .git, could still get code execution on the runner. Fix: validate .git against an allowlist of expected config keys, or delete everything in .git/config except a minimal set (remote and core basics), and reject .git/info/attributes. Alternatively, restore only the objects and packs and regenerate config and hooks.
findings.title: Restored-.git sanitizer is a denylist; other config keys can still execute code during checkout
